Operation Cyclone was the CIA's program to arm and fund the Afghan mujahideen against the Soviet army, one of its largest covert operations. It began under Jimmy Carter in July 1979 with small, non-lethal aid and grew after the Soviet invasion and under Reagan.

Its scale rose from tens of millions of dollars a year to several hundred million by the late 1980s, with Saudi Arabia matching US money. Total US spending is usually put at a few billion dollars over the decade.

The US never dealt with the fighters directly. Weapons went to Pakistan, where General Zia ul-Haq's government and its ISI decided which parties received them, and favoured Islamist groups such as Hekmatyar's. Congressman Charlie Wilson pushed Congress for more money. From 1986 the program supplied Stinger anti-aircraft missiles.

It was part of the Reagan Doctrine of backing anti-communist movements in the Cold War. Its legacy is argued over: it helped drain the Soviet Union, but it also left armed Islamist networks in the region.
